Working notes:

- Do not default to option C. It was rejected on 9/10 requests because C was not a valid option or was not offered.
- Only select options explicitly shown in the ticket’s option list.
- Option A = standard queue; option B = priority desk. Option C appears to represent a regional office when available, but its label is sometimes truncated.
- The sole successful case was REQ-2405: large shipment from the north region, with C available, and C was accepted. This suggests C may be correct when the request explicitly offers a matching regional-office route.
- Request size, type, region, sender, and message hints alone are not yet sufficient to establish a reliable A/B rule.
- Before acting, verify the complete option text and whether the requested region matches any regional-office option. If C is absent, choose only A or B; never invent C.

Working notes:

- Option labels: A = standard queue, B = priority desk, C = regional office (often truncated). Verify the full text before acting.
- New evidence shows C is not valid merely because the request has a matching region or mentions a regional office.
- Accepted C cases: REQ-2405 (large north shipment), REQ-2410 (large north claim), REQ-2411 (small north claim), and REQ-2417 (small north claim). The newer successes suggest C may often apply to north-region claims, but REQ-2405 prevents treating that as an exclusive rule.
- Rejected C cases: REQ-2412 (north invoice), REQ-2413 (south refund), REQ-2414 (east claim), REQ-2415 (east refund), and REQ-2419 (east invoice).
- A was rejected for REQ-2416 (small north shipment) and REQ-2418 (large east invoice); therefore A is not a safe fallback when C is uncertain.
- B has not yet been tested successfully or unsuccessfully in these examples; do not assume it is correct without stronger evidence.
- Request size, type, region, sender, urgency, and message wording alone do not establish a reliable general A/B/C rule.
- Before acting, inspect the complete option text and seek an exact precedent for the request’s type and region. If no reliable precedent exists, avoid inventing or assuming an option.
